text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Four people died and some 500 Bulgarian towns and villages were left without power due to heavy snowstorms and extremely cold weather in the past two days.

-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to vote on the resignation of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's Socialist government at an extraordinary session today. Videnov announced the resignation at a party congress on December 21. @

-- The current cabinet should submit to parliament by the year's end a draft budget and a privatisation programme for 1997 and a package of laws, introducing a currency board system in the country, the Socialist parliamentary group decided.
-- An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission is expected to arrive in Sofia in the first days of January, the IMF resident office in Sofia said.
-- Bulgaria's president elect Petar Stoyanov who is due to take office in January said he did not rule out the possibility of an interim cabinet as a way out of the current government crisis.

-- The oldest Russian-made first reactor at Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power plant is expected to be connected to the national electricity grid between January 15-20, the plant's information centre said.
The National Electric Company is expected to name by January 10 the company which it had chosen to upgrade the plant's 1000-megawatt fifth and sixth reactors. @
-- Bulgaria's national carrier Balkan Airlines will not service domestic and international flights on January 1, the airline's press centre said.

-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 7.3 billion levs to 162.7 billion levs between November 30 and December 17 which is around 79 percent of the revised annual target, finance ministry said.
-- Bulgaria's Industry Ministry had sold sold firms worth some two billion levs in the first 11 months, the Privatisation Agency said.
-- The women's Olympic champion and world high jump record holder Stefka Kostadinova was voted Bulgaria's athlete of the year. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
